channel.title: Wisconsin Newspaper Association - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Newspaper Association (wnanews.com)

item.title: Cabin Fever Cures: Indoor adventures for the winter
item.description: Wisconsin has the cure for cabin fever and its restlessness, the urge to get out and do something new.

item.title: Missing out on farm pay day
item.description: My farming days are over but a recent story made me realize that I clearly left a lot of money on the table.

item.title: Group alleges Port Washington city officials violated open meetings law
item.description: The nonprofit group behind several lawsuits against the City of Port Washington and the failed recall of the city’s mayor has taken another legal action against the city, alleging violations of Wisconsin’s Open Meetings Law.

item.title: Funding the First Years and Beyond: Options to raise revenue for child care
item.description: As the availability and affordability of child care has become an increasingly pressing issue, most potential options in Wisconsin to generate new child care revenue are available at the state -- rather than the local – level.

item.title: NNA disappointed with SCOTUS decision in USPS v. Konan
item.description: The recent Supreme Court of the United States ruling in USPS v. Konan delivers a significant setback for newspapers and other businesses that rely on the nation’s mail system -- narrowing the ability to hold the United States Postal Service accountable for service failures.

item.title: 2026 WNA Convention takes place March 5-6 in Madison
item.description: The 2026 WNA Annual Convention will take place March 5-6 at the Madison Concourse Hotel & Governor's Club in Madison.

item.title: Village of New Glarus files complaint over EMS records
item.description: The Village of New Glarus is filing a complaint with with the Green County District Attorney for records the New Glarus Area EMS has refused to share with the village.

item.title: Complaint against Clintonville school board president released
item.description: The complaint against Glen Drew Lundt, president of the Clintonville Board of Education -- which resulted in an investigation by an independent counsel and Lundt being censured by the board -- has been released.

item.title: Wisconsin Watch teams with Journal Sentinel to provide Fact Briefs
item.description: Ahead of another pivotal election year, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel and Wisconsin Watch are teaming up to produce more Fact Briefs, 150-word answers to yes/no questions based on claims made in the info sphere.

item.title: Brandon Wegner joins Iron County Miner
item.description: Brandon Wegner has joined the Iron County Miner in Hurley as a contributor.
